summary: HTTP-level verification of Authorization SSOT (core/authz) + object-level user guards against LIVE preview backend. 26/27 tests pass. Confirmed: P0-SEC-USERS closed (accountant 403 on all /api/users CRUD, admin 200 on GET), privilege escalation blocked (accountant POST /api/users role=admin → 403), destructive admin-only enforced on /api/financial-reset/* and /api/biz-accounts/cleanup, ledger perms honored (accountant edit=allowed, delete=403), settings mutation blocked for accountant, admin self-guards work (cannot self-delete or self-role-change → 403), no regressions on read endpoints (both roles 200 on /vehicles /customers /operations /finance/journal-entries /stats), unauth → 401, no 5xx from middleware. STRICT NON-DESTRUCTIVE: only GETs and rejected (401/403/410/422) requests were sent; no mutations persisted. Uncovered ONE defense-in-depth regex gap in core/authz.py (see rca).

minor.issue: core/authz.py destructive_admin regex '^/api/[^?]*(/cleanup|/purge|/wipe|/danger|...)' requires a literal '/' before 'cleanup' but /api/ already consumes it, so top-level /api/cleanup, /api/purge, /api/wipe, /api/danger paths bypass the SSOT and reach the handler. Today the only such route (DELETE /cleanup/keep-debts-only) is a hardcoded 410 legacy stub, so there is NO current data-loss risk — but ANY future /api/cleanup|purge|wipe|danger endpoint would be unprotected by the middleware.

action_items: core/authz.py: tighten destructive_admin regex to also cover TOP-LEVEL paths. Current: r'^/api/[^?]*(financial-reset|/reset$|/reset-|reset-financial|/cleanup|/purge|/wipe|/danger)'. Suggested: r'^/api/([^?]*/)?(financial-reset|reset$|reset-|reset-financial|cleanup|purge|wipe|danger)' — i.e., make the leading '/' before the keyword OPTIONAL so /api/cleanup/... /api/purge/... /api/wipe/... /api/danger/... are all matched. Re-run tests/test_authz_ssot_http_iter362.py::TestDestructiveAdminOnly::test_top_level_cleanup_regex_gap after the fix; it should turn green (accountant 403 instead of 410).
critical_code_review_comments: core/authz.py destructive_admin regex has a subtle boundary bug — alternation branches that start with '/' (e.g., '/cleanup') never match top-level paths of the same name because '^/api/[^?]*' consumes the URL up to and including that slash. Recommend using a word-boundary / optional-prefix pattern for defense in depth.

rca of the issue.issue: Top-level /api/cleanup|purge|wipe|danger paths bypass the destructive_admin authorization rule.
rca of the issue.root_cause: In core/authz.py the regex 'r"^/api/[^?]*(financial-reset|/reset$|/reset-|reset-financial|/cleanup|/purge|/wipe|/danger)"' anchors '^/api/' (consuming the slash), then '[^?]*' greedily matches path segments, and finally requires the alternation. Branches like '/cleanup' expect a literal '/' immediately before 'cleanup', but for /api/cleanup/... the only slash before 'cleanup' is the one already consumed by '^/api/', so there is nothing left for the branch to match. Branches without leading slash (financial-reset, reset-financial) still work at top level.
rca of the issue.reproduction: curl -X DELETE -H 'Authorization: Bearer <accountant_token>' 'https://<preview>/api/cleanup/keep-debts-only?confirm=x' → 410 (accountant reached handler). Expected: 403 from ASGI authz middleware.
rca of the issue.mitigation: Make the '/' before each keyword optional and/or use a segment-boundary regex. Example: r'^/api/(?:[^?]*/)?(financial-reset|reset$|reset-|reset-financial|cleanup|purge|wipe|danger)(?:/|$)'. After patch, re-run TestDestructiveAdminOnly::test_top_level_cleanup_regex_gap — it should pass. No data-loss risk currently because the only exposed route (DELETE /cleanup/keep-debts-only) is a legacy 410 stub, but this is a P1 defense-in-depth fix to prevent future regressions.
